researchBoundaries.transfer: identity is distinct from mutable state
persisted representation is evidence for reconstruction, not identity authority
logical entity, runtime, image, checkpoint and execution identities must not collapse
birth is one-time and later continuity advances the same lineage
accepted successors bind exact predecessors and conflict cannot resolve by recency alone
immutable realization identity is distinct from logical identity
later interpretation does not rewrite source identity
locator and realization are not object identity
later readings and graph relations preserve prior identities

candidateLaws.title: Identity is not mutable state
candidateLaws.rule: A logical Record identity must remain distinct from lifecycle state, editorial status, maturity, visibility and other mutable properties.

candidateLaws.title: Persistence is not identity authority
candidateLaws.rule: A file, row, serialized object or stored byte sequence may carry evidence for reconstruction but must not become authoritative identity merely by existing.

candidateLaws.title: Logical identity is not revision identity
candidateLaws.rule: RecordId must identify one logical entity across time while RevisionId must identify one exact accepted immutable revision.

candidateLaws.title: Kind is constitutive
candidateLaws.rule: RecordKind must be fixed at birth. A change of ontological kind creates a distinct Record and an explicit relationship rather than mutating the original kind.

candidateLaws.title: Birth occurs once
candidateLaws.rule: A RecordId may be admitted at most once. Later states are lineage successors, not repeated births of the same identifier.

candidateLaws.title: Continuity requires predecessor binding
candidateLaws.rule: An accepted successor revision must name and validate the exact predecessor required by the Record lineage.

candidateLaws.title: Conflicts fail closed
candidateLaws.rule: Incompatible successors must remain an explicit conflict and must not be resolved solely by updatedAt, file order, commit recency or route precedence.

candidateLaws.title: Identifiers are never reused
candidateLaws.rule: Once admitted, a RecordId remains globally reserved even if the Record is withdrawn, archived or tombstoned.

candidateLaws.title: Locator is not identity
candidateLaws.rule: Routes, slugs, filenames and external handles are locators that resolve Records and must not define ontological identity.

candidateLaws.title: Aliases preserve historical binding
candidateLaws.rule: A locator that has publicly identified one Record must not later be silently reassigned to a different Record; migration uses an explicit alias or historical boundary.

candidateLaws.title: Revision order is not truth order
candidateLaws.rule: A later revision is temporally later but is not automatically more correct, more supported or epistemically superior.

candidateLaws.title: Source survives interpretation
candidateLaws.rule: Later review, reading, summary or claim must not rewrite the identity or immutable content of the source Record it interprets.

candidateLaws.title: References have logical and pinned modes
candidateLaws.rule: The identity system must distinguish a logical RecordRef from a PinnedRecordRef bound to one exact RecordId and RevisionId.

candidateLaws.title: Representation does not mint identity
candidateLaws.rule: Changing framework, renderer, storage adapter, file location, serialization, route realization or build output must not create a new logical Record identity by itself.

candidateLaws.title: Relations do not rewrite endpoints
candidateLaws.rule: A graph edge may relate Records but must not mutate, replace or retroactively redefine the identities of its subject or object.
